column1: Whereas GDP measures the total income produced domestically, GNP measures the total income earned by nationals (residents of a nation). For instance, if a Japanese resident owns an apartment building in New York, the rental income he earns is part of U.S. GDP because it is earned in the United States. But because this rental income is a factor payment to abroad, it is not part of U.S. GNP. In the United States, factor payments from abroad and factor payments to abroad are similar in size—each representing about 4 percent of GDP—so GDP and GNP are quite close.
